title: Gut Microbial Metabolites and Intestinal Permeability in Patients With Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation Undergoing Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Intervention
official: MicrobIal Metabolites and Gut Leakiness assessmeNT in Patients With sevEre Tricuspid reGuRgItation Undergoing Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve inTervention: a Multidimensional analYsis (INTEGRITY-Trial)
summary: Emerging evidence highlights a bidirectional gut-heart axis, particularly relevant in patients with right heart failure. Elevated right atrial pressures and systemic congestion may impair intestinal perfusion and compromise epithelial integrity, leading to increased gut permeability ("leaky gut") and translocation of microbial products. These processes can trigger systemic inflammation and exacerbate cardiac dysfunction. Alterations in the gut microbiome-collectively referred to as dysbiosis-have also been linked to heart failure pathogenesis. However, the role of intestinal barrier dysfunction and microbial signatures in patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) remains largely unexplored.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* • Patients with functional tricuspid regurgitation (TR) who were evaluated for transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention

  * Written informed consent in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and local legislation
  * Patients undergoing PFO closure without any other known comorbidities will serve as control group

Exclusion Criteria:

* • Previous tricuspid valve repair or replacement

  * Echocardiographic evaluation not available or not suitable for analysis at baseline
  * Key information from patients (e.g. NYHA, TR grade) not available
  * Known allergy or intolerance against the studied device
  * Persons held in an institution by legal or official order
